fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. The people say Absalom, the man they anointed, has died in battle. Then comes the question: “So why do you say nothing about restoring the king?” It's like a whole room full of people all thinking the same thing, and nobody wants to be the first to say it out loud.

Nobody here is shopping for a new king. Absalom is the one they anointed, and he has died in battle. What the people ask is why nobody is saying anything about restoring the king, and that king is David.

Commander is the word. David says, “…if from now on you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab!” Amasa, who led Absalom's army (2 Samuel 17:25), is being given Joab's place. That's a big wow, even for a stamper with a mustache.
That's the message. The men of Judah send word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.” Six words and the whole mood flips. After all that arguing, that's the sweetest text David could get.
Judah isn't telling David to wait. They send word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.” No waiting on a vote from anybody. It's an invitation to come back.
Nobody's blocking the road. The men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and escort him across the Jordan. Their message to him said, “Return.” You don't send that and then slam the gate.

No handoff of Amasa here. The men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and escort him across the Jordan. Amasa's new place as commander was part of a message David sent, not a delivery. The Jordan crossing is all about getting David home.
Yes, baker. Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, came down along with a thousand men of Benjamin. He didn't come alone. That's a whole crowd at the river with him.
It's true, actually. Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down along with a thousand men of Benjamin. They came along with him. So don't picture one lonely man at the river.

That's him. Ziba, the steward of the house of Saul, rushed down to the Jordan with his fifteen sons and twenty servants. That's thirty-six people if you count Ziba, which is a whole crowd heading for one river. He wasn't coming by himself.

Good eye, baker. Shimei says, “For your servant knows that I have sinned…” He speaks of his wrongdoing on the day the king left Jerusalem. No excuses, no spin. That's about the hardest sentence to say out loud.
The priests aren't part of this answer. David sent a message to them earlier, but here he says, “Am I not indeed aware that today I am king over Israel?” He's speaking for himself, as king.
That's the word. The king says to Shimei, “You shall not die.” Shimei had fallen down before the king, and these are the words he gets. I think that's a sentence he'll remember for a long time.
